content: The medication is indicated for the treatment of cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in immunocompromised adults, including those with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). The induction therapy involves administering 5 mg/kg intravenously every 12 hours, infused over one hour, for a duration of 14 to 21 days. It is also indicated for the prevention of CMV disease in adult transplant recipients at risk for CMV. For this purpose, the induction therapy consists of 5 mg/kg intravenously once daily, infused over one hour, for 7 to 14 days. For primary or recurrent CMV infections, oral dosing of 1000 mg three times daily is recommended. For recurrent cases, intravenous dosing of 5 to 6 mg/kg, 5 to 7 times per week, may be used. Initial treatment should begin with ganciclovir at 5 mg/kg per dose intravenously every 12 hours. Once the therapy is tolerated, it can be transitioned to valganciclovir at 900 mg orally every 12 hours for 21 to 42 days or until symptoms resolve. For recurrent cases, 5 mg/kg intravenously once daily may also be used. Drug interactions with ganciclovir include the following: 1. Ganciclovir and Abacavir: Co-administration increases the risk of hematologic toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 2. Ganciclovir and Bacitracin: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent use with other nephrotoxic drugs. 3. Ganciclovir and Imipenem/Cilastatin: Co-administration may increase the risk of seizures. Avoid unless the potential benefit outweighs the risk. 4. Ganciclovir and Imipenem/Cilastatin/Relebactam: Similar to the above, co-administration may increase seizure risk. Avoid unless necessary. 5. Ganciclovir and Zidovudine: This combination is contraindicated due to increased toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. 6. Ganciclovir and Hydroxyurea: Co-administration may increase the risk of myelosuppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Ganciclovir and Didanosine: Co-administration increases toxicity due to decreased renal clearance. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 8. Ganciclovir and Doxorubicin (including liposomal formulations): Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ganciclovir and Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may lead to toxicity due to decreased renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Ganciclovir and Emtricitabine: Co-administration increases toxicity risk. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 11. Ganciclovir and Lamivudine: Co-administration increases hematologic toxicity risk. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 12. Ganciclovir and Mycophenolate: Ganciclovir increases mycophenolate levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 13. Ganciclovir and Peramivir: Co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 14. Ganciclovir and Pretomanid: Pretomanid inhibits OAT3, increasing ganciclovir levels. Monitor for adverse effects and consider dose adjustments. 15. Ganciclovir and Probenecid: Ganciclovir increases probenecid levels by competing for renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. 16. Ganciclovir and Amphotericin B: Co-administration increases toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor closely. 17. Ganciclovir and NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen, indomethacin, ketorolac): These drugs increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Monitor closely. 18. Ganciclovir and Vinblastine/Vincristine (including liposomal formulations): Co-administration increases toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor closely. In general, ganciclovir interacts with many drugs by increasing toxicity or altering renal clearance. Careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or alternative therapies may be required to minimize adverse effects.
